Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Jordan — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps.

Call recap:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for PII and transaction logs (legal requires that customer data never be co-mingled).
- KMS requirement: customer-managed keys / HSM preferred (FIPS 140-2/3).
- Network control: preference for traffic that does not leave their VPC; potential interest in an on-prem option for air-gapped workloads.
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 reports and audit logs are a must.
- Timeline: team target is production proof-of-concept in Q1 2027; procurement and security review happening this month.

High-level options we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest, but data is processed on shared infrastructure (not recommended given current isolation requirements).
- Dedicated capacity: dedicated GPU pools and tenant isolation for runtime; control plane remains Redwood-managed; good fit when you want predictable throughput but can accept a managed control plane.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full network-level isolation, optional private control plane or on-prem package, supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and stricter network egress controls.

Action items / next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Solutions Engineering + Security to validate KMS/HSM integration, audit log formats, and network topology (propose Wed 17 Nov, 10:00 AM PT).
2) I attached our Dedicated vs Private VPC one-pager and the SOC2/questions doc you requested for initial review.
3) If you can share the specific procurement checklist or any must-have controls (e.g., FIPS KMS, dedicated hardware requirement), we’ll map them to the two deployment modes.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the deep-dive and loop in our SEs.

—

Thanks Jordan — great questions. High-level answers below and a short checklist mapping your controls to each deployment mode.

Short answers:
- Dedicated capacity: provides tenant-isolated GPU pools (compute tenancy) and separate runtime instances per customer. It is not always physical hardware single-tenant by default; in many cases we provide strict tenancy at the hypervisor/container level on shared racks. If a hard requirement for single-tenant physical hardware exists, we can discuss a dedicated-hardware add-on (longer lead time & procurement).
- Private VPC / On-prem: provides network-level isolation (customer-managed VPC), optional private control plane, and on-prem deployments where no traffic traverses Redwood-managed networks. This is the recommended path when you need to guarantee that data never leaves your network and for full KMS/HSM control.

Checklist (meets/partial/needs add-on):
- Customer-managed KMS (FIPS 140-2): Dedicated = partial (customer KMS supported for keys but HSM co-location may be limited); Private VPC/On-prem = meets.
- No data egress from VPC: Dedicated = partial (we can minimize egress and encrypt; control plane calls may still be routed); Private VPC/On-prem = meets.
- SOC 2 evidence / audit logs: Both = meets (we provide SOC 2 and standard audit logs; Private VPC adds ability to ship logs directly to your collector).
- Physical single-tenant hardware: Dedicated = needs add-on (available as special configuration); Private on-prem = meets.
- Time-to-deploy estimate: Dedicated = 2–4 weeks for reserved capacity and config; Private VPC = 4–10 weeks (depends on networking and procurement); On-prem = 8+ weeks.

Recommended next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer (Alex Martinez) + Security (propose Wed 17 Nov, 10:00 AM PT). Alex will walk through KMS/HSM options and network topology.
2) Share your procurement checklist and any regulatory constraints so we can produce a gap analysis.
3) I attached the one-pager and SOC2 questionnaire for your security team to start.

If Helpful: I can prepare two short configs/cost sketches (Dedicated vs Private VPC) for your SRE/procurement team as a follow-up.

Thanks — will send calendar invite and loop Alex in.
